A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, references, and Appendices A–C. Their methods, proofs, and experiments can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic and real-world regression experiments in Figures 1–2, plus posterior-variance results in Appendix C.1 and Figure 3.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and results, including the supplementary posterior-variance evaluation.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and the sampling and constrained variance-reduction procedures in Equations (3)–(4) are unchanged. The new constraint discussion explains the existing procedure without modifying it.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic GP tasks, King County house sales, red wine quality, and Auto MPG datasets. The tested ambiguity radii and represented scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: RS, US, variance reduction, and EPIG remain the evaluated baselines, alongside the existing unconstrained DR variance-reduction ablation. v2 explains why Frogner et al. is excluded; it was not evaluated in v1 either.

E3.justification: The synthetic grid, kernels, noise, iteration budget, real-data preprocessing, hyperparameter-update schedule, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. The new statement that acquisition and evaluation use the same ambiguity radius documents the existing setup rather than revising it.

E4.justification: The unconstrained-versus-constrained ablation, comparisons across ambiguity radii, and Appendix C.1 posterior-variance analysis are retained unchanged. The added discussion supplies no new ablation or robustness evidence.

E5.justification: Figures 1–3 retain means and standard errors from 20 random trials involving initialization and algorithm randomness. No repeated-run information or uncertainty-estimation procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: Figures 1–3 contain identical plotted results, including their uncertainty displays. The corresponding performance findings remain unchanged, with no added, removed, or corrected result entries.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, lemmas, convergence theorems, Corollary 4.3, and proofs in Appendices A–B are unchanged. The added complexity and prior-work discussion introduces no new formal result or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: two distributionally robust GP active-learning methods, prediction-error guarantees, and empirical effectiveness.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 expands the constraint rationale and discusses cubic GP cost, scalable approximations, and their unresolved proof requirements. Section 6 explains the exclusion of Frogner et al. and revises the experimental interpretation, including EPIG's objective mismatch. These refine limitations and explanations already partly present in v1.

D1.justification: Section 6 newly specifies that the same ambiguity radius is used in the algorithm and performance measure. This is a limited reproducibility clarification; Appendix C's implementation details, dataset preparation, and access information remain substantively unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Hübotter et al. (2024), Liu et al. (2015), and Liu et al. (2020). It adds a focused comparison with Hübotter's theoretical guarantees, discussing submodularity and the stated convergence bound, while retaining the broader research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds explanatory paragraphs and the 'Necessity of Constraints' and 'Computational Complexity' headings, alongside grammar, spelling, author-name-order, and citation-style corrections. The overall section and appendix organization remains intact.

P2.justification: The three figures retain their plots, axes, and legends. Figure 1 moves earlier relative to the surrounding text, and Figures 2–3 correct 'columns' to 'rows'; Figure 2's caption also explicitly identifies expected squared error.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the retained work easier to assess through clearer computational limitations, experimental-design disclosures, baseline-selection rationale, and comparison with relevant theoretical prior work. Copy and caption corrections also help. These are limited improvements in transparency and positioning; the algorithms, proofs, and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
